title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models
role: Origin of the PoE noise-prediction sum this project composes with; states the conditional-independence assumption under which the interaction term is zero.
reads: The same noisy image x_t fed once per concept and once unconditionally, giving pixel-space noise predictions eps(x_t,t|c_i) and eps(x_t,t) at every step T to 1; conditions are label or coordinate embeddings fused with the time embedding, or GLIDE text prompts.
trains: Per-domain conditional diffusion models with 10% null-label dropout (CLEVR 30k images with one object coordinate, Relational CLEVR 50k with one relation, FFHQ 51k with attribute labels), 1000 steps cosine schedule, 750k iterations on CLEVR; plus binary evaluation classifiers on real images.
combines: eps_hat = eps(x_t,t) + sum_i w_i (eps(x_t,t|c_i) - eps(x_t,t)) at every step on a shared x_t; negation eps_hat = eps + w (eps(x_t,t|c_i) - eps(x_t,t|c_j~)).
adding: Valid if concepts are conditionally independent given x; the learned field may be non-conservative; fails as hybrids when objects are in the image center and when models come from different datasets.
noise_and_seed: not addressed; 5,000 generated images per test setting, no seed variance or error bars.
unseen: partly: concepts are all seen; held-out combinations of 2 and 3 concepts and up to 8 CLEVR objects where training images hold 1 to 5; accuracy falls 86.42 to 59.20 to 31.36% with 1, 2, 3 components.
headline: CLEVR 3-component accuracy (% of 5,000 images with every object found by a classifier, higher better) 31.36 vs 7.34 for EBM, a gap of 24.02 points; diffusion model trained from scratch with GLIDE code.
suggests: (inferred) The paper's own hybrid failures are product paths whose picture is one fused object, a ready test of whether a score-path encoder places a product path near the joint caption or near one concept; sum-lands-on-joint should fail exactly where conditional independence fails.
model: GLIDE-code pixel diffusion trained from scratch (CLEVR 128x128, FFHQ 64x64); pre-trained small GLIDE; Stable Diffusion in Fig. 1 only

extra_papers.title: Should EBMs model the energy or the score?
extra_papers.why: Trains a scalar energy on x_t whose gradient is the score field; a learned scalar readout of the score, cited as evidence a non-conservative eps is acceptable.

disagreements.paper_says: Caption says EBM's FID is 'much lower than other methods', but the table (44.41, 55.89, 58.66) and the text on p. 13 say EBM's FID is much worse.

disagreements.claim: Table 2 caption says the method 'achieves comparable or better results than baselines'
disagreements.paper_says: Its accuracy is below EBM in all three Relational CLEVR settings (60.40 vs 78.14, 21.84 vs 24.16, 2.80 vs 4.26).

disagreements.claim: CLEVR training images hold 1 to 5 objects
disagreements.paper_says: Fig. 14 caption says the training set contains images with fewer than five objects, while p. 8 says each image contains 1 to 5 objects.
